summary: This Wikipedia-derived note is a biography of George VI, King of the United Kingdom and the Dominions from 11 December 1936 until his death in 1952. It covers his accession and the disputes over his brother Edward's titles, his marriage to Elizabeth Bowes-Lyon, and the Second World War, including the Blitz and the family's wartime stay in London. It also traces the decline of the Empire, the end of the Indian imperial title, and Ireland's and India's moves toward republic status within or outside the Commonwealth.
one_line: Biography of King George VI, who reigned from 1936 to 1952, guided the monarchy through the Second World War, and became the first Head of the Commonwealth.
key_facts: George VI (Albert Frederick Arthur George; 14 December 1895 -- 6 February 1952) was King of the United Kingdom and the Dominions of the British Commonwealth from 11 December 1936 until his death in 1952.
George VI was the last Emperor of India and the first Head of the Commonwealth.
Albert assumed the regnal name "George VI" to emphasise continuity with his father and restore confidence in the monarchy.

George VI's first act as king was to confer on his brother the title "His Royal Highness The Duke of Windsor", but the Letters Patent creating the dukedom prevented any wife or children from bearing royal styles.
George VI was forced to buy the royal residences of Balmoral Castle and Sandringham House from Edward, because these were private properties and did not pass to him automatically.
Three days after his accession, on his 41st birthday, George VI invested his wife, the new queen consort, with the Order of the Garter.
On the day of the abdication, the Oireachtas removed all direct mention of the monarch from the Irish constitution, and the next day it passed the External Relations Act.
In September 1939, Britain and the self-governing Dominions other than Ireland declared war on Nazi Germany.
On 13 September 1940, two German bombs exploded in a courtyard at Buckingham Palace while the King and Queen were there.
The Queen declared: "I am glad we have been bombed. It makes me feel we can look the East End in the face."
In August 1942, the King's brother, Prince George, Duke of Kent, was killed on active service.
The title Emperor of India was abandoned in June 1948, Ireland left the Commonwealth in 1949, and India became a republic within the Commonwealth the following year.
In 1920 Albert met Lady Elizabeth Bowes-Lyon, who rejected his proposal in 1921 and 1922 before agreeing to marry him; they married in 1923.
George VI's elder daughter, Elizabeth, succeeded him as monarch.
During the war, U.S. First Lady Eleanor Roosevelt remarked on the rationed food served and the limited bathwater permitted during a stay at Buckingham Palace.

entities.role: Queen consort, wife of George VI, youngest daughter of the Earl and Countess of Strathmore and Kinghorne

entities.name: Sheila, Lady Loughborough

entities.name: Oireachtas
entities.role: Parliament of the Irish Free State, which removed direct mention of the monarch from the Irish constitution

entities.name: Irish Free State
entities.role: State whose parliament passed the External Relations Act after the abdication

entities.name: External Relations Act
entities.role: Irish act giving the monarch limited authority, on government advice, to appoint diplomatic representatives and be involved in foreign treaties

entities.name: Buckingham Palace
entities.role: Official London residence where the King and Queen stayed throughout the war and where bombs exploded in September 1940

entities.name: Windsor Castle
entities.role: Residence where the King and Queen usually spent nights during the war

entities.name: Balmoral Castle
entities.role: Royal residence George VI had to buy from Edward

entities.name: Sandringham House
entities.role: Royal residence George VI had to buy from Edward, where he died in 1952

entities.name: Nazi Germany
entities.role: Power Britain and the Dominions declared war on in September 1939

entities.name: Blitz on London
entities.role: German bombing campaign whose first night, 7 September 1940, killed about one thousand civilians, mostly in the East End

entities.name: Commonwealth of Nations
entities.role: Association into which the British Empire transitioned during George VI's reign; he adopted the title Head of the Commonwealth
